title: Order Intake and Charge Posting Rules — Laboratory Test Orders
content:
## Charge lines at placement

When a Laboratory Test Orders order is placed, one charge line with the reason *ordered* is posted for every test on the order, at that test's list price in the order's test menu. The order's list-price total is the sum of its charge lines less its credited lines. A test that is not in the order's test menu cannot be charged on that order.

## Reflex lines

Reflex lines (charge reason *reflex*) are posted by the laboratory only for classes that perform reflex testing, and only for the reflex test of a test already charged on the order, at the reflex test's list price. A patient or a provider cannot request a reflex line.

## Consumer-initiated orders

- A consumer-initiated order is accepted only for a service class that can be purchased without a requisition.
- The patient must be at least the class's consumer minimum age, in whole years, on the order date. The evidence is the date of birth on the patient's own record, not the caller's statement.
- A consumer-initiated order carries no more than the class's maximum number of tests per consumer order.
- It is always billed self-pay and prepaid at purchase, at the sum of the tests' self-pay prices plus the physician oversight fee where the requisition encounter places that fee on this order.

**Age at the boundary (abstract cases).** A patient who reaches the minimum age on the order date itself is at least that many whole years old and qualifies. A patient who reaches it on the day after the order date does not.

## Client billing

Client billing is available only for classes that allow it. Client billing is never allowed when the patient's coverage on the order date is Original Medicare Part B, because no class allows client billing for Original Medicare beneficiaries. The evidence is the payer class and status of the coverage on file.

| Patient's coverage on the order date | Class allows client billing | Client billing possible |
|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | Yes | No |
| Original Medicare Part B | No | No |
| Any other payer class | No | No |
| Any other payer class | Yes | Yes |

## Requisition validity and standing orders

A physician requisition must be collected within the class's requisition validity period, counted in calendar days from its order date. A standing order is accepted only for classes that accept standing requisitions. It is valid for the class's standing-order period, in calendar months from the order date, and for at most the class's maximum number of collections.

**Example (hypothetical).** A Routine Clinical Testing order for a Lipid Panel and a CBC posts two *ordered* lines, one at each test's list price, and its list-price total is their sum. If the CBC line is later credited, the total falls to the Lipid Panel's list price alone.
